implementation: independent IOService power-child lease and monotonic revocation protocol
native_evidence: explicit PM events fixture; never proof of an acquired Apple power domain

anchors: registerPowerDriver copies the supplied state table before submitting its PM request
addPowerChild establishes a real IOPowerConnection and asynchronously completes three dependent requests
changePowerStateToPriv requests this private child's desire without overwriting the IOPCIDevice nub's request
powerChangeDone is called after a completed transition; setPowerState entry alone is not completion
handleAcknowledgeSetPowerState accepts an acknowledgement while setPowerState is still in flight
PMstop sets PMStop and waits for prior PM driver callouts through waitForPMDriverCall, whose 15-second timeout is not an unconditional lifetime barrier
An independent guarded count retains the external revocation owner until every requestStop hook returns; finish refuses before closing when that count is nonzero
PMstop submits asynchronous tree detach through an IOPMRequest that retains its target IOService
requestPowerDomainState is an internal PM-workloop operation and returns success without acting when called outside that thread
IOPMPreventSystemSleep is a private undefined flag for third-party drivers; it is not used here
checkSystemSleepAllowed permits low-battery or thermal emergency sleep before evaluating ordinary sleep-prevention clamps

references.anchor: IOPCIDevice is itself power managed; a retained nub or a sampled PMCSR D0 bit is not a child's lifetime request
